lanes.title: Biblical history
lanes.source: Traditional chronology (early Exodus, from 1 Kings 6:1). Many scholars prefer later dates for the patriarchs and the Exodus.

lanes.title: United kingdom
lanes.source: Approximate; Saul's reign length is uncertain (Acts 13:21).

lanes.title: Kings of Israel
lanes.source: Reign dates after Edwin R. Thiele, The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings. Other systems differ by a few years; overlaps are co-regencies.

lanes.title: Kings of Judah
lanes.source: Reign dates after Edwin R. Thiele. Overlaps are co-regencies.

lanes.title: Prophets
lanes.source: Approximate periods of ministry from the books' headings.

lanes.title: Who was in power
lanes.source: Standard ancient Near Eastern chronology (middle chronology for Mesopotamia).

lanes.title: Rulers
lanes.source: Reign dates as usually given in histories of the ancient world.

lanes.title: Church history
lanes.source: Dates as commonly given in histories of the church.

lanes.title: Islamic history
lanes.source: Dates as commonly given in histories of Islam (Common Era); the Prophet’s birth and first revelation by Muslim tradition.

events.title: Call of Abraham
events.summary: Abram leaves Harran for Canaan at God's call, with the promise of land, offspring and blessing for all nations.
events.note: Traditional chronology; many scholars place the patriarchs a few centuries later.

events.title: Jacob's family settles in Egypt
events.summary: Joseph, now a ruler in Egypt, brings Jacob and his sons to Goshen during the famine.

events.title: The Exodus
events.summary: Moses leads Israel out of Egypt; Passover, the crossing of the sea and the covenant at Sinai.
events.note: Early date from 1 Kings 6:1. Many scholars prefer a 13th-century date (c. 1260 BC).

events.title: Entry into Canaan
events.summary: After forty years in the wilderness, Israel crosses the Jordan under Joshua.

events.title: Period of the judges
events.summary: Cycles of unfaithfulness, oppression and deliverance under leaders such as Deborah, Gideon and Samson.

events.title: Solomon's temple dedicated
events.summary: Built over seven years and dedicated with Solomon's prayer.

events.title: The kingdom divides
events.summary: The northern tribes reject Rehoboam and follow Jeroboam: Israel in the north, Judah in the south.

events.title: Fall of Samaria
events.summary: Assyria takes Samaria and deports the northern kingdom.

events.title: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem
events.summary: Assyria ravages Judah's towns, but Jerusalem is spared in Hezekiah's reign. Sennacherib's own annals also record the campaign.

events.title: Josiah's reform
events.summary: The Book of the Law is found in the temple; Josiah renews the covenant and removes idols.

events.title: First deportation to Babylon
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes Daniel and other young nobles to Babylon.

events.title: Jehoiachin taken to Babylon
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes the king, the court and Ezekiel into exile and sets up Zedekiah.

events.title: Jerusalem and the temple destroyed
events.summary: After a long siege Babylon burns the temple and deports much of Judah.

events.title: Cyrus's decree and first return
events.summary: Cyrus allows the exiles to go home and rebuild the temple; Zerubbabel leads the first return.

events.title: Second temple completed
events.summary: Finished in the sixth year of Darius after encouragement from Haggai and Zechariah.

events.title: Esther in Susa
events.summary: A Jewish queen of Persia saves her people from Haman's plot; the origin of Purim.

events.title: Ezra returns to Jerusalem
events.summary: Ezra the scribe brings a second group and teaches the Law.

events.title: Nehemiah rebuilds the walls
events.summary: Jerusalem's walls are rebuilt in fifty-two days despite opposition.

events.title: Maccabean revolt
events.summary: Judas Maccabeus leads the revolt against Antiochus IV; the temple is cleansed and rededicated, remembered at Hanukkah.

events.title: Herod begins rebuilding the temple
events.summary: A vast expansion of the second temple that was still under way in Jesus' day.

events.title: Birth of Jesus
events.summary: Born in Bethlehem in the days of Herod the Great, who died in 4 BC.

events.title: Ministry of Jesus
events.summary: Baptism by John, teaching and healing in Galilee and Judea, and the journey to Jerusalem.

events.title: Crucifixion and resurrection
events.summary: Jesus is crucified under Pontius Pilate at Passover and rises on the third day.

events.title: Pentecost
events.summary: The Holy Spirit is poured out; Peter preaches and about three thousand are baptised.

events.title: Paul's conversion
events.summary: On the road to Damascus, the persecutor Saul meets the risen Jesus.

events.title: Council of Jerusalem
events.summary: The apostles and elders agree that Gentile believers need not be circumcised.

events.title: Paul's missionary journeys
events.summary: Churches founded across Galatia, Macedonia, Greece and Asia.

events.title: Paul in Rome
events.summary: Under house arrest, Paul preaches freely for two years.

events.title: Revelation written
events.summary: John's visions on Patmos, traditionally dated to the end of Domitian's reign.
events.note: Some date it to the late 60s.

events.summary: King of Judah (the southern kingdom).

events.title: Manasseh

events.title: Amon

events.title: Jehoiakim

events.title: Jehoiachin

events.title: Zedekiah
events.summary: King of Judah (the southern kingdom).

events.title: Samuel
events.summary: Last of the judges; anoints Saul and David.

events.title: Nathan
events.summary: Confronts David after Bathsheba.

events.title: Elijah
events.summary: Challenges Ahab and the prophets of Baal on Carmel.

events.title: Elisha
events.summary: Succeeds Elijah; many miracles in Israel.

events.title: Jonah
events.summary: Sent to preach to Nineveh.

events.title: Amos
events.summary: A shepherd from Tekoa denounces injustice in Israel.

events.title: Hosea
events.summary: Pictures God's faithful love through his own marriage.

events.title: Isaiah
events.summary: Prophet in Jerusalem under Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah.

events.title: Micah
events.summary: Foretells a ruler from Bethlehem.

events.title: Nahum
events.summary: Announces Nineveh's fall.

events.title: Zephaniah
events.summary: Prophesies in Josiah's day.

events.title: Jeremiah
events.summary: Warns Judah for forty years and promises a new covenant.

events.title: Habakkuk
events.summary: Asks how God can use Babylon; 'the righteous shall live by faith'.

events.title: Daniel
events.summary: Serves in the Babylonian and Persian courts.

events.title: Ezekiel
events.summary: Visions among the exiles by the Chebar canal.

events.title: Haggai
events.summary: Urges the returned exiles to rebuild the temple.

events.title: Zechariah
events.summary: Visions of restoration and a coming king.

events.title: Malachi
events.summary: The last Old Testament prophet.

events.title: John the Baptist
events.summary: Preaches repentance and baptises Jesus.

events.title: Egypt: Middle Kingdom
events.summary: A reunited Egypt; trade and building at home and abroad.

events.title: Old Babylonian kingdom
events.summary: Amorite dynasty of Babylon; Hammurabi unifies Mesopotamia.

events.title: Hittite empire
events.summary: Anatolian power that rivalled Egypt; fought at Kadesh in 1274 BC.

events.title: Egypt: New Kingdom
events.summary: Egypt's imperial age: Thutmose III, Akhenaten, Ramesses II.

events.title: Philistine city-states
events.summary: Sea Peoples settled on the coast: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron, Gath.

events.title: Aramean kingdom of Damascus
events.summary: Israel's frequent northern rival until Assyria took Damascus.

events.title: Neo-Assyrian empire
events.summary: Dominates the Near East; destroys Samaria and besieges Jerusalem.

events.title: Neo-Babylonian empire
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon conquers Judah.

events.title: Persian (Achaemenid) empire
events.summary: From Cyrus to Darius III; allows the exiles to return.

events.title: Alexander the Great
events.summary: Conquers Persia, Egypt and the east; Greek language and culture spread.

events.title: Ptolemaic rule over Judea
events.summary: Judea governed from Alexandria; the Septuagint is translated there.

events.title: Seleucid rule over Judea
events.summary: Ruled from Antioch; Antiochus IV bans Jewish practice.

events.title: Hasmonean kingdom
events.summary: Independent Jewish state under the Maccabees' heirs.

events.title: Roman Republic in the east
events.summary: Pompey takes Jerusalem in 63 BC.

events.title: Herod the Great
events.summary: Rome's client king of Judea; massive building projects.

events.title: Roman Empire
events.summary: From Augustus to the fall of the West.

events.title: Byzantine (Eastern Roman) empire
events.summary: Rome's eastern half, ruled from Constantinople.

events.title: Islamic caliphates
events.summary: Rapid expansion across the Near East, North Africa and Spain.

events.title: Ottoman empire
events.summary: Rules the Holy Land from 1517 to 1917.

events.title: Hammurabi
events.summary: King of Babylon, known for his law code.

events.title: Thutmose III
events.summary: Egypt's great warrior pharaoh; some link him with the oppression in Exodus.

events.title: Ramesses II
events.summary: Long-reigning pharaoh; often linked with the Exodus by those who hold a late date.

events.title: Shishak (Shoshenq I)
events.summary: Pharaoh who raided Judah after Solomon.

events.title: Tiglath-pileser III
events.summary: Assyrian king who made Israel and Judah pay tribute.

events.title: Sargon II
events.summary: Completed the deportation of Israel.

events.title: Sennacherib
events.summary: Besieged Jerusalem under Hezekiah.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar II
events.summary: Captured Jerusalem and destroyed the temple.

events.title: Cyrus the Great
events.summary: Founder of the Persian empire; freed the exiles.

events.title: Darius I
events.summary: Confirmed the temple decree.

events.title: Xerxes I (Ahasuerus)
events.summary: The king of Esther.

events.title: Artaxerxes I
events.summary: Sent Ezra and Nehemiah.

events.title: Antiochus IV Epiphanes
events.summary: Desecrated the temple in 167 BC.

events.title: Augustus
events.summary: First Roman emperor; ordered the census of Luke 2.

events.title: Tiberius
events.summary: Emperor during Jesus' ministry.

events.title: Pontius Pilate
events.summary: Prefect of Judea who sentenced Jesus.

events.title: Claudius
events.summary: Expelled Jews from Rome.

events.title: Nero
events.summary: Persecuted Christians after the fire of AD 64; Paul and Peter martyred by tradition.

events.title: Vespasian and Titus
events.summary: Crushed the Jewish revolt and destroyed Jerusalem.

events.title: Domitian
events.summary: Emperor at the traditional date of Revelation.

events.title: Trajan
events.summary: Corresponded with Pliny about Christians.

events.title: Diocletian
events.summary: Launched the Great Persecution.

events.title: Constantine
events.summary: First Christian emperor; called the Council of Nicaea.

events.title: Theodosius I
events.summary: Made Nicene Christianity the state religion.

events.title: Justinian I
events.summary: Built Hagia Sophia; codified Roman law.

events.title: Charlemagne
events.summary: Crowned emperor in Rome in AD 800.

events.title: Henry VIII
events.summary: Broke with Rome; head of the Church of England.

events.title: Charles V
events.summary: Holy Roman Emperor at the Diet of Worms.

events.title: Code of Hammurabi
events.summary: One of the oldest written law codes, carved on a basalt stele.

events.title: Late Bronze Age collapse
events.summary: Empires fall across the eastern Mediterranean; the Sea Peoples appear.

events.title: Phoenician alphabet
events.summary: Ancestor of the Hebrew, Greek and Latin alphabets.

events.title: First Olympic Games
events.summary: Held at Olympia in Greece.

events.title: Founding of Rome
events.summary: The traditional date.

events.title: Homer's epics
events.summary: The Iliad and the Odyssey take written form.

events.title: Library of Ashurbanipal
events.summary: Thousands of clay tablets at Nineveh, including the Gilgamesh epic.

events.title: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
events.summary: Traditional dates; many scholars place him about a century later.

events.title: Confucius
events.summary: Chinese teacher whose sayings shaped East Asian thought.

events.title: Roman Republic founded
events.summary: Rome expels its last king.

events.title: Parthenon built
events.summary: The temple of Athena on the Athenian Acropolis.

events.title: Death of Socrates
events.summary: The Athenian philosopher is executed.

events.title: Septuagint begun
events.summary: The Hebrew Scriptures translated into Greek at Alexandria.

events.title: Qin unifies China
events.summary: Qin Shi Huang becomes the first emperor of China.

events.title: Dead Sea Scrolls copied
events.summary: The Qumran scrolls, the oldest surviving Hebrew Bible manuscripts.

events.title: Julius Caesar assassinated
events.summary: The end of the Roman Republic draws near.

events.title: Great Fire of Rome
events.summary: Nero blames the Christians.

events.title: Destruction of the Second Temple
events.summary: Roman legions under Titus destroy Jerusalem.

events.title: Pompeii destroyed
events.summary: Vesuvius buries Pompeii and Herculaneum.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.summary: The last Western emperor is deposed.

events.title: Muhammad's Hijra
events.summary: Beginning of the Islamic calendar.

events.title: Gutenberg's printed Bible
events.summary: Movable-type printing transforms the spread of books.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.summary: The Ottomans take the Byzantine capital.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.summary: The first of four voyages.

events.title: Clement of Rome writes to Corinth
events.summary: One of the earliest Christian writings outside the New Testament.

events.title: Ignatius of Antioch martyred
events.summary: Writes seven letters on his way to death in Rome.

events.title: Polycarp martyred
events.summary: Bishop of Smyrna and a disciple of John.

events.title: Justin Martyr's First Apology
events.summary: Describes Christian worship and defends the faith to the emperor.

events.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies
events.summary: A refutation of Gnosticism that appeals to the apostolic tradition.

events.title: Tertullian
events.summary: First major Latin theologian; coins the term 'Trinity' (trinitas).

events.title: Origen
events.summary: Alexandrian scholar; the Hexapla and On First Principles.

events.title: Decian persecution
events.summary: The first empire-wide persecution.

events.title: Great Persecution
events.summary: Diocletian orders churches and Scriptures destroyed.

events.title: Edict of Milan
events.summary: Constantine and Licinius grant religious toleration.

events.title: Council of Nicaea
events.summary: Rejects Arianism; the first form of the Nicene Creed.

events.title: Athanasius lists the 27 New Testament books
events.summary: His Easter letter is the earliest list matching today's New Testament.

events.title: Council of Constantinople
events.summary: Affirms the deity of the Holy Spirit; the Nicene Creed takes its familiar form.

events.title: Jerome's Vulgate
events.summary: The Latin Bible used in the West for a thousand years.

events.title: Augustine of Hippo
events.summary: Confessions, City of God; deeply shapes Western theology.

events.title: Council of Chalcedon
events.summary: Christ confessed as one person in two natures.

events.title: Rule of St Benedict
events.summary: Foundation of Western monasticism.

events.title: East–West Schism
events.summary: Mutual excommunications divide Rome and Constantinople.

events.title: The Crusades
events.summary: Military campaigns to the Holy Land.

events.title: Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae
events.summary: Synthesis of Aristotle and Christian theology.

events.title: Wycliffe Bible
events.summary: First complete English Bible, translated from the Vulgate.

events.title: Jan Hus burned
events.summary: Czech reformer condemned at the Council of Constance.

events.title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
events.summary: The start of the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Schleitheim Confession
events.summary: Early Anabaptist statement of faith.

events.title: Augsburg Confession
events.summary: The chief Lutheran confession.

events.title: Act of Supremacy
events.summary: Henry VIII becomes head of the Church of England.

events.title: Calvin's Institutes
events.summary: First edition of the Reformed classic.

events.title: Council of Trent
events.summary: The Catholic response to the Reformation.

events.title: Heidelberg Catechism
events.summary: A widely used Reformed catechism.

events.title: First Baptist congregation
events.summary: John Smyth's English exiles in Amsterdam.

events.title: King James Version
events.summary: The Authorized Version of the English Bible.

events.title: Synod of Dort
events.summary: Reformed response to the Remonstrants.

events.title: Westminster Confession
events.summary: Confession of English and Scottish Presbyterianism.

events.title: First Great Awakening
events.summary: Revivals under Edwards, Whitefield and the Wesleys.

events.title: Wesley's Aldersgate experience
events.summary: A turning point in the beginnings of Methodism.

events.title: Azusa Street revival
events.summary: Los Angeles revival at the start of modern Pentecostalism.

events.title: Second Vatican Council
events.summary: Reforms in Catholic worship and relations with other churches.

events.title: Birth of Muhammad
events.summary: Born in Mecca, by Muslim tradition.

events.title: First revelation
events.summary: Muslims hold that the Quran began to be revealed to Muhammad in the cave of Hira.

events.title: The Hijra
events.summary: Muhammad and his followers move from Mecca to Medina; year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

events.title: Battle of Badr
events.summary: First major battle between the Muslims of Medina and the Quraysh of Mecca.

events.title: Conquest of Mecca
events.summary: Muhammad returns to Mecca; the Kaaba is cleared of idols.

events.title: Death of Muhammad
events.summary: Dies in Medina.

events.title: Rashidun caliphate
events.summary: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali lead the Muslim community.

events.title: Jerusalem surrenders to Umar
events.summary: The city passes from Byzantine to Muslim rule.

events.title: Uthman’s copy of the Quran
events.summary: Caliph Uthman has a standard text of the Quran copied and sent to the main cities.

events.title: Umayyad caliphate
events.summary: Ruled from Damascus; the empire reaches from Spain to Central Asia.

events.title: Battle of Karbala
events.summary: Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, is killed; a defining moment for Shia Islam.

events.title: Dome of the Rock
events.summary: Built in Jerusalem on the Temple Mount.

events.title: Abbasid caliphate
events.summary: Ruled from Baghdad; a golden age of learning.

events.title: Umayyad emirate of Córdoba
events.summary: Al-Andalus: Muslim rule in Spain, later a caliphate.

events.title: House of Wisdom, Baghdad
events.summary: Greek, Syriac and Persian works are translated into Arabic.

events.title: Saladin retakes Jerusalem
events.summary: Ends the crusader kingdom’s rule of the city.

events.title: Mongols sack Baghdad
events.summary: End of the Abbasid caliphate in Baghdad.

events.title: Ottoman Empire
events.summary: From Anatolia to the Balkans, the Middle East and North Africa.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.summary: Mehmed II takes the city; it becomes the Ottoman capital.

events.title: Fall of Granada
events.summary: End of Muslim rule in Spain.

events.title: Mughal Empire
events.summary: Muslim dynasty ruling much of the Indian subcontinent.
